assessments.reasoning: The autotools mirror serves GNU Libtool’s maintenance document at commit 6d7ce133ce54898cf28abd89d167cccfbc3c9b2b. Its footer names the Free Software Foundation, Inc. as copyright holder. Receipt 60a8898e4fcf45928aebb057dc1e5d85 records the claimed SHA-256 139d092a4336557923dcbfb917ec4422feed1c6e24f324aeccf86c662aea17ab. Section 9.4 supplies the project name for the clause, its intended header and its operative permission in one passage.

Software Commons License Index’s SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 defines an exception as an additional permission or documented modification and requires separate support for affected editions. It assigns crosswalk decisions to the index and authority over instruments to their publishers. This supports the editorial use of “active” and the exception category. Receipt e55dd065846d4e4497ae6133f9276c3d identifies the inspected revision.

challenge.method: Applied SCES §§1–4 on proposition-specific authority, exact revisions, scope and adversarial review of identity merges. Following protocol stage 7, reopened the sources and tested whether §9.4 could instead be HACKING’s own license, a project-wide rule, or the Libltdl header in §9.5.
challenge.results: Section 9.1 explicitly lists HACKING under notice preservation, and the file’s closing copyright notice grants copying and distribution on that condition. Section 9 introduces several licensing forms. Section 9.5 addresses Libltdl sources and names the GNU Lesser General Public License in the exception itself. These passages rule out all three broader readings and leave the §9.4 identity intact.

limitations: The witness is the maintenance template at the supplied 2.4.7 source revision. The connector retrieved HACKING by commit and matched the claimed file digest. The supplied sources contain no separate GNU Git tag object for independently checking the tag-to-commit association.
Application to another file requires that file’s notice and evidence. HACKING §1 describes the instructions as outside the release distribution.

The review used SCES-1.0 at ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710. The adopted bundle SHA-256 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce was supplied with the task. The three policy receipts identify the individual documents.
reasoning: GNU Libtool’s HACKING §9.4 names the “Libtool exception clause” and gives maintainers the header for the libtool script generated from ltmain.in. The permission is conditional. If someone distributes the covered file as part of a program or library built using GNU Libtool, they may include that file under the same distribution terms they use for the rest of that program. This supports the registry’s editorial mapping to an active exception named “Libtool Exception.” The project supplies the instrument and the index owns the classification.
